text.checkText: Re-inspect the room after the fix: the item passes.

zones.name: Entrance
zones.meaning: The first metre decides the guest's first impression: a marked door or a dead key card light is seen before anything else.
moves: Start every room at the door, with the guest's eyes: handle, frame, light, floor.
Put a cloth for the door and the frame on every trolley, so it is not skipped.
Report a slow door closer or a weak lock the same day: it is a safety item.
zones.question: What does the guest see in the first five seconds after the door opens?

zones.name: Bed
zones.meaning: The bed is why the guest pays for the room. A hair or a stain on the linen is a complaint, often a refund.
moves: Check the linen in daylight before it goes on the bed, not after.
Send stained or damaged linen back to the laundry with a tag, so the pattern is seen.
Show the bed standard with a photo at the linen room: corners, pillows, throw.
zones.question: Where does the linen come from, and who looks at it before it goes on the bed?

zones.name: Bathroom
zones.meaning: The bathroom is where guests look closest and where most rooms fail: hair, lime and water spots are seen at once.
moves: Finish the bathroom with a last look from the door at floor height: drain, corners, behind the toilet.
Give every trolley its own drain tool and a dry microfibre cloth for the last wipe.
Plan descaling of showers by floor, so lime does not wait for a complaint.
zones.question: Which part of the bathroom does the attendant look at last, and how much time is left for it?

zones.name: Desk and wardrobe
zones.meaning: Dust on the desk and items left in the drawers tell the guest that nobody really looked.
moves: Open every drawer and the safe in every checkout room, every time.
Wipe the remote and the switches with disinfectant: they are touched most.
Keep a hanger and amenity count on the trolley list, so gaps are filled at once.
zones.question: What did the last guest leave behind that we found, and what did we not find?

zones.name: Minibar and amenities
zones.meaning: A missing cup or an empty coffee box is small for us and the first call to reception for the guest.
moves: Fill the trolley from a par list per room type, not from memory.
Place amenities the same way in every room, so a gap is seen at a glance.
Agree with the minibar team who checks and who refills, and when.
zones.question: Which item runs out first on the trolley, and why?

zones.name: Windows and balcony
zones.meaning: Streaks on the glass and a curtain off its hooks are seen in the evening light, when the guest is in the room.
moves: Look at the glass from an angle against the light before you leave.
Run each curtain once to the end and back: it shows a broken hook at once.
Report every window or balcony door that does not lock: it is a safety item.
zones.question: When were the windows of this floor last cleaned outside, and by whom?

zones.name: Smell and air
zones.meaning: Smell is the first thing a guest notices and the hardest to fix later. Smoke or damp fails the room on its own.
moves: Open the window at the start of the clean, not at the end.
Send a smoke smell to the supervisor at once: the room needs an ozone or deep clean, not perfume.
Run water in every drain of a room that was empty for days.
zones.question: What does the room smell like when the door has been closed for an hour?

zones.name: General
zones.meaning: The floor, the lights and the small damages: what the guest sees as the state of the whole hotel.
moves: Vacuum from the far corner to the door, edges first.
Switch every light on once during the clean, not only the main light.
Report damage with a photo the same day, so maintenance can plan the part.
zones.question: Which damage do we walk past every day because it has always been there?

tips: Check the room before reception sells it. Mark only what you see now: pass, fail or n.a.; a failed critical item fails the room on its own.
Scan the QR code on the door or type the room; mark the faults, then “Mark the rest as pass”. Five minutes is enough for a standard room.
Every fault goes back to someone: the attendant cleans it again, maintenance fixes it. Maintenance items go to the Action Tracker when you save.
A low first-time pass rate of one attendant asks for a walk through a room together, a clearer standard or more minutes per room, never for a name on the wall.
Copy a checklist and adapt the items and weights to your brand standard; save it as a template file for the other hotels of the group.
